battle.name: 第二次卡洛斯戰爭
battle.brief: 一八四六年五月起，馬德里的軍事起事被平定後，內戰迅速蔓延到北部的納瓦拉、阿拉瓦與比斯開，卡洛斯派以村落為堡壘與自由派軍隊對抗三年。卡面雷管步槍是政府軍步兵的制式裝備，也是卡洛斯山區民兵最渴望的走私品，兩者的差別最終不在槍而在封鎖線與法國的干預。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰的兩方是西班牙自由派王國與卡洛斯派。自由派一方以女王伊莎貝二世的名義執政，一八四六年由攝政的瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂納主持政府，軍權則集中於「和平者」巴爾多梅羅·埃斯帕特羅將軍手中；北方戰區由政府軍各師團與補充民兵組成，配有野戰炮兵與工兵，另有依一八四四年法令編成的民警衛隊巡邏鄉村、封鎖山區小徑，這套由本地線人與崗哨構成的網絡正是卡洛斯游擊隊最忌憚的東西。卡洛斯派是內戰遺留的王位正統主義運動，以費爾南多七世之弟卡洛斯·馬利亞·德·拉·波爾博恩為正統依歸，後由其姪卡洛斯六世承襲；支持者集中於納瓦拉、阿拉瓦、比斯開與阿拉貢北部，多為農莊民兵、村落壯丁與退役軍官，另有本篤會與耶穌會士在精神與情報上襄助。卡洛斯派在納瓦拉設有自己的「王室」與軍令序列，編制分為正規營、骨幹游擊大隊與地方徵召民兵三層，並以「人民戰爭」的名義在村鎮層面徵稅、徵兵、審判。一八四八年卡洛斯方面組成的「皇家遠征軍」企圖翻越比利牛斯山回到納瓦拉，是這場戰爭最後一次大規模的野戰企圖。裝備上卡洛斯派缺炮少彈，攻擊多靠人數與地形；自由派則握有制式步槍、火炮、攻城器材與英國借款支撐的財政，靠封鎖與遠征消耗對方。
countriesEn: The two sides were the liberal Kingdom of Spain and the Carlists. The liberal side governed in the name of the child queen Isabella II: in 1846 executive power lay with the regent Maria Christina, while military authority was concentrated in the hands of Baldomero Espartero, the Pacificator. The northern theatre was made up of the government's divisions with their militia supplements, field artillery and engineers attached, and the Guardia Civil, created by law in 1844, patrolled the villages and sealed the mountain tracks; its network of local informants and posts was exactly what the Carlist bands feared. The Carlist side was the legitimist dynastic movement left over from the earlier civil war, holding that the crown passed to Carlos María de la Borbón, brother of Ferdinand VII, and after him to his nephew Carlos VI. Its support lay in Navarre, Álava, Biscay and northern Aragon, mostly farm militia, village levies and former officers, with Benedictine and Jesuit clergy supplying spiritual backing and intelligence. The Carlists maintained their own royal court and chain of command in Navarre, built in three layers, regular battalions, a core of guerrilla bands and locally summoned militias, and at village level they levied taxes, raised men and dispensed justice under the banner of a war of the people. The Royal Expedition assembled by the Carlists in 1848, which tried to cross the Pyrenees back into Navarre, was the last large attempt at open battle in this war. In equipment the Carlists were short of guns and ammunition, and their attacks rested on numbers and ground; the liberals held service muskets, artillery, siege trains and a treasury backed by British loans, and wore the enemy down with blockade and expeditions.
people: 巴爾多梅羅·埃斯帕特羅是自由派的柱石，一八三六年以「和平者」之名鎮壓第一次卡洛斯戰爭並受封「勝利公爵」，此後擔任攝政與陸軍最高指揮者，一八四六年北線的每一次圍剿都由他定奪；他對山區的嚴厲手段同時又加深了當地的敵意。一八四六年五月二日，馬德里的奧唐奈與塞拉諾將軍率部起事響應卡洛斯派，幾小時內被鎮壓平定，隨即成為自由派用來鎮壓北方的口實。卡洛斯一側：六月初納瓦拉的胡安·德·薩瓦拉起兵，最先在潘普洛納把全面戰火點燃；一八四七年起馬爾克斯·德·拉·聯松接掌北線，一八四八年由何塞·馬里亞·德·奧爾貝（人稱「牧師」）率領「皇家遠征軍」翻越比利牛斯山，卻在文塔·德埃查瓦里一帶連遭挫敗；阿拉瓦山區的「阿拉馬奧茨神父」安東尼奧·奧爾特利斯以一支不大的隊伍在山中游擊多年，最終在一八四八年被政府軍包圍擊斃。自由派方面，拉蒙·瑪麗亞·納爾瓦埃斯與萊奧波爾多·奧多尼爾在政治上輪替掌權，一八四八年推翻埃斯帕特羅的攝政；法國方面，路易·拿破崙·波拿巴派遣的「西方軍團」在布熱奧與烏迪諾指揮下於一八四八至五〇年間入西班牙援助伊莎貝二世，這是歐洲國家直接出兵干涉西班牙內政的罕見先例。
peopleEn: Baldomero Espartero was the pillar of the liberal side. He suppressed the first Carlist war in 1836 under the title of the Pacificator, was ennobled as duke of Victory, and served afterwards as regent and as the supreme commander of the army; every encirclement in the northern theatre in 1846 was his decision, and the severity he showed the mountains only deepened local resentment. On 2 May 1846 Generals O'Donnell and Serrano rose in Madrid in support of the Carlists, were put down within hours, and thereby became the pretext the liberals used for crushing the north. On the Carlist side, Juan de Zavala raised the standard in Navarre in early June and first set the whole war alight at Pamplona; from 1847 the Marquis de la Unión took over the northern command, and in 1848 José María de Orbe, called the Pastor, led the Royal Expedition over the Pyrenees only to be beaten near Venta de Echavarri. In Álava the priest of Aramaotz, Antonio Ortells, harried the mountains for years with a small band and was finally surrounded and killed by government troops in 1848. On the liberal side Ramón María Narváez and Leopoldo O'Donnell alternated in power, and in 1848 they overturned Espartero's regency. On the French side, the army of the West sent by Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte, under Bugeaud and Oudinot, entered Spain between 1848 and 1850 to support Isabella II, a rare case of a European state intervening directly in the civil wars of another.
kits: 卡面這件雷管步槍在一八四六年前後已是西班牙步兵的標準槍械。法國在一八四〇年換裝的雷管步槍射程遠、底火不受潮霧影響，經馬德里政府引進並由西班牙兵工廠仿製，成為一八四二年式步兵雷管步槍；但各營士兵手上仍混有舊式燧發與火繩滑膛槍，北方邊區的守備單位常是後者。卡洛斯派的山地部隊大量使用獵槍（escopeta）、卡賓槍與截獲的政府軍步槍，其火力的重要來源之一是翻越法境的走私：法國邊境城鎮的軍火商把雷管步槍運過比達索阿河，在「漁夫島」一帶轉交，再由熟悉山徑的走私者分送各村。一八四八年皇家遠征軍甚至隨軍攜帶數百支新式雷管步槍與數門十二磅炮，可見卡洛斯方面在裝備上並非全無能力，缺的是後續的補充。炮兵是最不對稱的一環：自由派軍有完整的野戰炮兵連與攻城火炮，圍剿時能把封鎖線上的堡壘逐個壓平；卡洛斯派全境只能維持十餘門分散火炮，多是繳獲的六磅與四磅炮，平時藏山村與修道院。騎兵方面，自由派有國王騎兵團與騎炮兵，卡洛斯派則以農莊騎手組成游擊隊，來去如電而不列陣。運輸與補給同樣懸殊：政府靠新建道路與大車隊把糧彈運到前線，卡洛斯派靠牛車與人力背運沿山徑轉運，冬季雪封山口時常常斷糧。
kitsEn: The percussion rifle on this card was already the standard infantry arm of Spain around 1846. The French pattern of 1840, with its longer reach and a primer that fired in damp fog, was imported by the Madrid government and copied in Spanish arsenals, becoming the 1842 pattern infantry percussion musket; all the same, ranks were still mixed with older flintlock and matchlock smoothbores, and the frontier garrisons of the north were often armed with them. The Carlist mountain bands used large quantities of shotguns, carbines and captured government muskets, and one of their main sources of firepower was smuggling across the French border: arms dealers in the French border towns moved percussion muskets over the Bidasoa, handed them over on the Fishermen's Island, and had them carried on by smugglers who knew the tracks. The Royal Expedition of 1848 even carried several hundred new percussion muskets and a number of twelve-pounder guns into the field, so the Carlists were not wholly without means; what they lacked was resupply. Artillery was the most lopsided element of all: the liberal army had complete field batteries and siege guns and could batter down the blockhouse fortresses one by one, while the Carlists could keep barely a dozen scattered guns, mostly captured six- and four-pounders hidden in mountain villages and monasteries. In cavalry the liberals had the royal dragoon regiments and horse artillery, whereas the Carlist mounted men were farm horsemen in bands that rode in and out and never fought in line. Transport and supply were just as uneven: the government moved grain and powder to the front along new roads and in great wagon convoys, while the Carlists shifted them along mountain paths on ox-carts and on men's backs, and in winter, when snow closed the passes, their supply line often broke altogether.
tactics: 卡洛斯派的戰法是「人民戰爭」式的游擊與襲擾：一支小隊夜間沿山徑移動，天亮前以一次齊射衝擊政府軍的行軍縱隊或駐紮哨所，打完即散，取捨存亡全靠對地形的熟悉與隨手可用的掩體，核心是速度而不是陣線。卡洛斯方面從不與政府軍打正面會戰，除非對方彈藥耗盡或脫離掩體。一八四六年七月初在納瓦拉的巴拉斯奧因，自由派縱隊在晨霧中遭多面射擊而崩潰，埃斯帕特羅於是改採圍堵：把敵方據點逐個孤立，切斷村鎮間聯繫，以炮兵射擊堡壘外圍，再在缺口處集中步兵。納瓦拉重鎮埃斯特利亞自一八四六年起被圍，卡洛斯的「王室」先後遷入城內，此後遷往奧爾杜尼亞，使北方形成一個與馬德里並存的權力中心。政府另一套手段是封鎖：海軍巡邏比斯開沿岸與比達索阿河口，攔截輸入卡洛斯方面的軍火，並以海上封鎖配合陸路推進，試圖切斷山區的糧道與武器來源。一八四八年的皇家遠征軍試圖以一次強行越嶺扭轉戰局，結果因糧秣與彈藥不足，在文塔·德埃查瓦里一帶被擊退，說明卡洛斯派即使有正面作戰的意願，也缺乏支撐它的後勤。到一八四九年，雙方的勝負都靠夜色、掩體和剩餘彈藥來決定。
tacticsEn: The Carlist way of war was a war of the people fought by harassment and ambush: a small band moved along the tracks at night, fell on a government column or a garrison just before dawn with a single volley, and dispersed, surviving on knowledge of the ground and whatever cover lay to hand; the essential quality was speed, not line formation. The Carlists would not accept a general engagement on equal terms unless the enemy had run out of ammunition or lost its cover. At Barásoain in Navarre in early July 1846 a liberal column was broken by fire from several directions in the morning mist, and Espartero switched to encirclement: isolating each rebel position one by one, cutting the links between villages, shelling the works from the guns, and then concentrating infantry at the breach. The important town of Estella was under siege from 1846, and the Carlist court moved into the town and later to Orduña, creating in the north a centre of power parallel to Madrid. The government's other instrument was the blockade: the navy patrolled the Biscay coast and the mouth of the Bidasoa, stopping arms from reaching the Carlists, and the maritime blockade was tied to the advance on land in an effort to cut the mountain supply lines. The Royal Expedition of 1848 tried to reverse the situation with a single forced crossing of the mountains, and was driven back near Venta de Echavarri for want of food and powder, which showed that even when the Carlists wanted a general action they lacked the logistics to support one. By 1849 the issue on both sides was decided by night, by cover and by what ammunition remained.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下：戰爭自一八四六年五月延續到一八四九年，前後約三年，最後的停戰安排延至一八五〇年。自由派北方軍在高峰期約有三萬至四萬人，另有民兵與騎兵補充；卡洛斯派的武裝人數常被估為三萬至四萬，但真正受過操練、能列陣作戰的骨幹只有數千人，其餘多為按村鎮徵召的民兵。炮兵對比最為懸殊：政府軍在北方可投入數十門六磅、八磅與十二磅野戰炮及攻城火炮，卡洛斯派全境長期只有十餘門可用火炮。一八四六年巴拉斯奧因戰役中，自由派方面陣亡與重傷合計約二千人，卡洛斯方面的損失相對有限。一八四八年皇家遠征軍規模約三千至四千人，跨越比利牛斯山後在文塔·德埃查瓦里一帶損失慘重，不到兩個月便解體。法國「西方軍團」在一八四八至五〇年入境的兵力約二萬五千人，其中一部分長期駐紮北部省分，專門堵截卡洛斯方面的國際軍火通道。武器方面，一八四二年式雷管步槍是政府軍步兵的制式裝備，卡洛斯方面在山區同時流通著燧發滑膛槍、獵槍與繳獲的雷管步槍，各年各地比例不同，並無可靠統計。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war ran from May 1846 to 1849, about three years, with the final arrangements for a truce stretching into 1850. The liberal army in the north numbered about thirty to forty thousand men at its height, with militia and cavalry supplements. The Carlist armed strength is often estimated at thirty to forty thousand as well, but only a few thousand were trained enough to fight in line; the rest were levied village by village. The artillery contrast was the sharpest of all: the government could bring dozens of six-, eight- and twelve-pounder field guns and siege pieces into the north, while the Carlists could hold barely a dozen serviceable guns for the whole country. At Barásoain in 1846 the liberal side counted about two thousand dead and wounded, while Carlist losses were comparatively light. The Royal Expedition of 1848 numbered some three to four thousand men and, after crossing the Pyrenees, suffered heavy losses near Venta de Echavarri and came apart in under two months. The French army of the West that entered Spain between 1848 and 1850 amounted to about twenty-five thousand men, part of it garrisoned for long periods in the northern provinces solely to close the international arms route. In weapons, the 1842 pattern percussion musket was the standard issue of the liberal infantry, while in the mountains the Carlists had flintlock smoothbores, shotguns and captured percussion muskets in circulation together, in proportions that varied by year and district and were never reliably counted.
cause: 起因是多層的。第一層是王位問題：一八三〇年代西班牙的王位繼承出現雙重合法性，自由派擁立女王伊莎貝二世及其母攝政，卡洛斯派則主張王冠應由費爾南多七世之弟卡洛斯一系承襲，兩邊的較量本質上是兩個王朝方案的對撞。第二層是宗教與地方特權：一八三四年耶穌會被解散，一八三六至三七年梅恩迪薩爾的教產還俗令關閉大量修道院並沒收其產業，天主教會在山區的機構與經濟受損，庇護院與傳教站在村鎮中的存在被削弱，卡洛斯派遂以「保護教會」凝聚鄉村。第三層是中央集權與地方特權的衝突：自由派政府推行全國一致的兵役與法制，取消巴斯克與納瓦拉的古老特權，並在山區修路、駐軍、徵收特別稅；農莊階層的抗拒把全村百姓推入卡洛斯一方，無須多少宣傳。第四層是直接的導火線：一八四六年五月二日馬德里的軍事起事被迅速平定，原本分散的不滿匯入北方，六月胡安·德·薩瓦拉在納瓦拉的響應遂成為全面開戰的訊號。而第一次卡洛斯戰爭留下的埃斯特利亞「王室」與未落實的停戰條款，使雙方都清楚對方不會放棄王位主張，談判因此無從進行。
causeEn: The causes ran in several layers. The first was the question of the crown. In the 1830s the Spanish succession produced two competing claims to legitimacy: the liberals stood behind the child queen Isabella II and her regent mother, while the Carlists held that the crown should pass to the line of Carlos, brother of Ferdinand VII, so that the contest was in truth a collision between two dynastic programmes. The second was religion and local privilege. The Jesuits were suppressed in 1834, and the Mendizábal disentailment of 1836-37 closed a great many convents and seized their property; the institutional and economic footing of the Catholic church in the mountains was cut away, monasteries and mission stations lost their place in the villages, and the Carlists gathered the countryside under the banner of protecting the faith. The third was the collision between centralisation and provincial fueros. The liberal government pushed a uniform conscription and a uniform legal order, abolished the ancient privileges of the Basque provinces and Navarre, built roads and stationed troops in the mountains, and levied special taxes; the resistance of the farming population pushed whole villages into the Carlist camp without much need for persuasion. The fourth was the immediate occasion. The military rising in Madrid of 2 May 1846 was put down swiftly, and the discontent it had gathered poured north instead, where Juan de Zavala's response in Navarre in June became the signal for general war. And because the first Carlist war had left the Carlist court at Estella and an unfulfilled truce, both sides understood that the other would never abandon its claim to the crown, so no settlement could be negotiated.
impact: 影響是深遠的。軍事上，這是一場十九世紀歐洲少數要靠外國軍隊直接介入才收場的內戰，法軍到來使自由派得以在北方扭轉局面，也讓卡洛斯方面明白國際干預是最後一張牌；同時它把一八四〇年代的技術下放到山區——雷管步槍比火繩槍射程更遠、受潮不易失效，農莊民兵只要一支好槍就能在遠距離造成殺傷，這種「一槍一兵」的普及改變了山區戰爭的成本結構，並為此後西班牙各地的游擊與武裝留下裝備前提。政治上，自由派的勝利並未帶來穩定，反而把西班牙推向軍人干政的循環：埃斯帕特羅的攝政、納爾瓦埃斯的倒戈、奧多尼爾的反覆倒戈，一八四八年革命之後自由派本身分裂，一八五四年維卡爾瓦革命推翻佩德羅一世，一八六八年革命又推翻伊莎貝二世。法制上，北方問題的懸而未決使地方特權與軍隊編制的爭議一直拖到一八七六年，才由加諾瓦斯·德爾卡斯蒂略的戰役收束。軍事理論上，這場戰爭提供大量游擊對正規軍的實例，被後來的技術兵種研究反覆引用。
impactEn: The consequences were far-reaching. Militarily this was one of the few civil wars in nineteenth-century Europe that had to be ended with foreign troops in the country: the arrival of the French army let the liberals reverse the situation in the north, and at the same time showed the Carlists that foreign intervention was their last card. The war also pushed the technology of the 1840s down into the mountains. The percussion rifle outranged the matchlock and fired reliably in wet weather, so a farm boy with one good gun could kill at long range; that spread of one shot, one man changed the cost structure of mountain warfare and left an equipment inheritance for the irregular bands that followed in every later Spanish conflict. Politically the liberal victory brought no stability, and instead pushed Spain into a cycle of military rule: Espartero's regency, Narváez's turn, O'Donnell's rising, the split of the liberals themselves after the revolution of 1848, the Vicálvaro revolution of 1854 that brought down Pedro I, and the revolution of 1868 that brought down Isabella II. In law the unresolved northern question kept the arguments about provincial fueros and military organisation alive until 1876, when they were settled by the campaign of Cánovas del Castillo. In military theory the war supplied a large body of cases of irregular warfare against regular troops, cited again and again in the later study of technical branches.
result: 結果是自由派靠封鎖、外國援助與消耗戰換來三年戰果，卻沒有在戰場上取得一次徹底的決定性勝利。一八四八年皇家遠征軍在文塔·德埃查瓦里一帶的慘敗，是卡洛斯方面最後一次大規模反攻的終點；此後戰事退化成山區的小規模遭遇與游擊，北方據點被逐一孤立。一八四九年西班牙革命推翻埃斯帕特羅後，自由派重新組軍，最終以一八五〇年的門德哈爾協約同仍在活動的卡洛斯首領拉蒙·卡夫雷拉達成局部停戰，北方的主要戰線自此平靜。然而卡洛斯派的王位主張並未廢除，埃斯特利亞的「王室」與其印璽、鑄幣及徵召制度一直維持到一八七六年，第三次卡洛斯戰爭才以另一場王位戰爭的方式徹底終結。整場戰爭的帳面是：卡洛斯派在游擊戰中佔優，自由派在封鎖與炮兵上佔優，最終的勝負由法國的介入與西班牙國內政治的變化決定，而不是由任何一場會戰決定。
resultEn: The result was three years of gains for the liberals bought with blockade, foreign aid and a war of exhaustion, without a single decisive victory on the field of battle. The defeat of the Royal Expedition near Venta de Echavarri in 1848 was the end of the last large Carlist counter-offensive; after it the war shrank into small encounters and ambushes in the hills, and the northern positions were isolated one by one. The revolution of 1849 in Spain swept Espartero away, the liberals rebuilt their armies, and the Convention of Mondéjar in 1850 brought a local truce with Ramón Cabrera, who was still active, and the main northern front went quiet. Yet the Carlist claim to the crown was not abandoned: the court at Estella, its seals, its coinage and its levies endured until 1876, when the Third Carlist War closed the question for good. The ledger of the whole war runs like this: the Carlists were superior in the skirmish, the liberals in the blockade and the artillery, and the outcome was decided by French intervention and by the shifting politics of Spain itself rather than by any engagement.
